title: A0 load and store frame theorem
statement: A successful A0 load leaves complete memory unchanged; a successful store changes exactly the addressed word-sized byte range to the little-endian source bytes; and a trapped load or store preserves complete memory.

formal.statement: For each w in {8,16,24,32,40,48,56,64}, arbitrary byte and presence arrays, base, value, and probe satisfy the A0 load validity/value law and pointwise atomic store frame law.

scope: Eight separate fixed-width array/bit-vector theorems covering every byte array, finite-domain presence array, word-valued effective address, stored word, and probe address. This is not an arbitrary-width induction theorem.

evidence.note: Concrete and symbolic access share the same domain-parametric orchestration. Replay rebuilds each source assertion, re-derives array elimination and select congruence, confirms deterministic DIMACS, and checks DRAT and LRAT. Committing a tentative sparse write on failure makes the width-16 negation satisfiable and changes byte 65535 from 00 to cd in the mutated path while encoded A0 traps and preserves memory.
